French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old French maladie.

Pronunciation

[edit]

  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Paris)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -i

Noun

[edit]

maladie f (plural maladies)

  1. illness, disease

Middle English

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • maladi, malady, maladye, maledye, malodye

Etymology

[edit]

From Old French maladie.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /malaˈdiː(ə)/, /ˈmaladiː(ə)/, /ˈmalədiː(ə)/

Noun

[edit]

maladie (plural maladies)

  1. A malady, disease, or illness; that which makes one sick or ill.
  2. Distress or anguish caused by love; the state of being lovesick.
  3. Iniquity, immorality, wickedness; that which is wrong or against nature.
  4. (rare) A lesion or wounding; the result of being hurt or injured.
  5. (rare) Torment or agony; the experience of being harmed mentally.
  6. (rare) A disturbance or sickness of the mind or brain.

Descendants

[edit]
  • English: malady

References

[edit]
  • “maladī(e, n.”, in MED Online, Ann Arbor, Mich.: University of Michigan, 2007, retrieved 10 December 2018.

Norman

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old French maladie.

Noun

[edit]

maladie f (plural maladies)

  1. (Jersey, medicine) illness

Derived terms

[edit]
  • maladie au r'nard (“malingering”)
  • maladie d'chucre (“diabetes”)
  • maladie d'la fontaine (“eczema”)
  • maladie d'nèrfs (“nervous breakdown”)
  • maladie d'rîngnons (“Bright's disease”)
  • maladie du fain (“hay fever”)
  • maladie malinne (“hysteria”)

Related terms

[edit]
  • malade (“ill”)

Old French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

malade (“sick, ill”) +‎ -ie

Noun

[edit]

maladie oblique singular, f (oblique plural maladies, nominative singular maladie, nominative plural maladies)

  1. sickness; illness
